title: Year-to-year control of hypoxia off the Pearl River Estuary
judge: Codex, single judge; procedure in benchmarking/evaluation/CODEX_JUDGE.md

scoring.split: framing 10, data 10, answer 20, mechanism 20, robustness 15, breadth 15, insight 10

anchors.0: Answers a different or vaguer question; no testable framing.
anchors.2: Operational definitions are given, but only one explanation is considered, or hypotheses are not tied to predictions.
anchors.4: Precise operational definitions; competing hypotheses with distinguishing predictions that structure the analysis.

anchors.0: Data mishandled (units, masks, grid, time or depth conventions) in a way that changes the results.
anchors.2: Correct handling, but the data's fitness for this question (model versus ocean, record length, resolution, missing variables) is not examined.
anchors.4: Correct handling, and fitness for this question is checked explicitly (for example against known observations or by internal consistency), with its consequences for the conclusions stated.

criteria.title: Quantitative answer against the answer key

anchors.0: Key quantities are missing, or wrong relative to the frozen answer key.
anchors.1: Quantities are reported, but most disagree with the answer key and no stated definition explains the difference.
anchors.2: About half of the answer-key items used by this criterion agree within tolerance (or differ only by a stated definition that the evaluator recomputed).
anchors.3: Most items agree within tolerance; one is missing or outside tolerance.
anchors.4: All answer-key items used by this criterion agree within tolerance, and their uncertainty is stated.

anchors.0: Description only, or process evidence contradicted by independently computed reference diagnostics.
anchors.1: A mechanism asserted from literature or intuition without a test in the supplied fields.
anchors.2: One candidate explanation tested; alternatives or identifiability limits not examined.
anchors.3: Quantitative process, conditional or lagged tests consistent with reference diagnostics; at least one alternative tested; unresolved causal attribution stated.
anchors.4: Competing explanations tested with quantitative diagnostics and uncertainty, consistent with independent references; data-supported conclusions and unresolved alternatives clearly distinguished; depth probes addressed. A justified inability to identify a dominant cause can receive full credit.

anchors.0: No sensitivity tests and no uncertainty.
anchors.2: One sensitivity test, or statistics that ignore short or autocorrelated records.
anchors.3: Several targeted sensitivity tests and suitable statistics; some key numbers lack uncertainty.
anchors.4: Targeted sensitivity tests on every choice that could change the conclusion (thresholds, baselines, regions, definitions), statistics suited to short and autocorrelated records, and uncertainty on all key numbers.

anchors.0: A single isolated diagnostic, with no link to related processes or published work.
anchors.1: Related processes or literature are mentioned but not used.
anchors.2: More than one variable or time scale is used, or results are compared with the literature, but mostly descriptively.
anchors.3: Processes or scales are connected and results are compared with published work with correct citations; one breadth probe is addressed well.
anchors.4: Scales and processes are connected (for example seasonal to interannual, physics to biogeochemistry), several variables are used coherently, agreement and disagreement with published work are stated with correct citations, and the breadth probes are addressed.

anchors.0: No clear answer to the question.
anchors.2: A clear answer, with generic limits and next steps.
anchors.4: A clear, quantified answer; precise limits of what the data can and cannot settle; specific next analyses or data that would settle the open points; at least one non-obvious insight supported by the analysis.

items.procedure: Yearly May-September hypoxic area-days and volume-days (oxygen below 62.5 mmol/m3) on the shelf box about 112.5-115.5 E, 21-22.8 N; first and last hypoxic day.
items.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: Spearman at least 0.7; timing +/-10 days)

items.procedure: Using core oxygen, temp, salt, chlorophyll, u and v, compare yearly hypoxia with stratification, plume area, surface chlorophyll, bottom temperature and along-shelf currents. Rank associations using correlations, partial correlations and contrasting-year or within-season composites, with uncertainty appropriate for ten autocorrelated years. Chlorophyll is a supply proxy; oxygen decline or an unclosed budget residual is not measured biochemical consumption. Associations alone do not establish a dominant cause.
items.oracle: Independent reference diagnostics from C_CORE fields bound to this task
items.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: robust associations consistent with independent references under matched definitions; tied or unstable rankings accepted when justified by uncertainty)

items.procedure: Yearly centroid of the hypoxic area relative to the estuary mouth (west versus east).
items.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: direction exact)

depth_probes: Separates evidence for stratification, chlorophyll as an organic-matter-supply proxy, and circulation or residence-time proxies.
Handles collinearity with conditional analyses or contrasting-year composites and reports unstable rankings.
Tests within-season timing and episodic ventilation from oxygen, density and current changes; does not infer a specific storm or wind reversal from currents alone.
States how missing discharge, nutrients and native oxygen-budget terms limit attribution; net oxygen decline and budget residuals are not measured respiration.
breadth_probes: Links to the synoptic mechanisms reported for this shelf and to hypoxia on other river-dominated shelves.
gates: A number or citation that cannot be traced (to executed analysis, outputs or a real source) is unsupported; the criterion it supports scores at most 1, and a flag is recorded.
A different target (region, period or quantity) without justification: Q and M score at most 1.
No executed analysis of the supplied data: every criterion scores 0, except F at most 1.
